r8d.title: Fuel Pump r2 painted now, then r3's crane and hose, then its light (r1 accepted)
r8d.note_html: Already run on 19 October; replaced by R8e above (do not paste it again). Buildings lane. Branch art/325-fuel-pump (exists, head 25ba21e2 or later). Issue #325. Follows R8c, reviewed on 18 October: r1 attempt 12 passes every test and is accepted. r3 attempt 9 got the light right but came back squat with a two-post crane, because one edit was asked to change three things at once. r2 was never painted, because R8c held it back until r3 passed. So R8d paints r2 now, on r0 and the accepted r1, then fixes r3 from attempt 7 in two steps with one change each: the crane and the hose first, with the house locked in pixels, then the light, with attempt 9 as the light reference.

c4e.title: Coaling stage r1 and r3 on the oblong guides, matching the accepted r0 and r2 (2 pictures)
c4e.note_html: Buildings lane. Branch art/325-buildings-v2 (exists, head c2b648e2 or later; art/325-fuel-pump is the Fuel Pump's, not the coaling stage's). Issue #325. Replaces C4d, which is off the page: all nine of its attempts failed on 18 October (Codex paints the stage 15 to 26 per cent wider than the plinth, and the fit then shrinks it low). Changed 19 October after the author's review 2: r0 and r2 are good, so only r1 and r3 are painted (six calls, three attempts a view) and they must match r2; the prompt puts the accepted r2 (raw attempt 8) back in the queue and does not repaint it. The guides are the oblong ones of #524 (Art's fuel_stop-oblong-r1 to r3), on the branch claude/art-guides-windmill-coaling, not merged yet; the prompt tells Codex to read them out of that branch into a folder outside its checkout. It carries the width limit (plinth 516 px of the guide, 632 of 1254; painted at most 5 per cent wider, 542 and 663), the walls' feet ratio, the long side per view, and the r3 winch opening, and measures the pier span before the fit. Nothing is stretched or bent: the angles come from the painting.
c4e.label: C4e
c4e.next: Coaling stage r1 and r3 on the oblong guides, matching the accepted r0 and r2 (branch art/325-buildings-v2, issue #325). Six calls at most.

c17c.title: Windmill body without sails, in the game's camera, on the new block-out (1 picture)
c17c.note_html: Buildings lane, after C4e. Branch art/461-windmill-sails (exists, head beed486 or later). Issue #461. The author found the demo's windmill wonky and asked for a repaint so it can be animated. The accepted body was seen from 19° down instead of the game's 30°, with its door and shaft turned about 27° off, so the sails could not sit on it. C17c paints the tower again, without sails, as an edit of Art's block-out in the game's own projection (on develop, assets/source/buildings-v2/guides/, PR #490), and records the hub point. The sail cross from C17b is kept. Every number is measured from the foot's width: camera, height, shaft slope, hub, door. Near-white pixels alone do not fail a picture; Art caps them at packing. Decided on 18 October: all four views are painted. C17c paints the front view r0; C17d follows it with r3, r1 and r2.
c17c.label: C17c
c17c.next: The windmill's tower without sails, front view r0 (branch art/461-windmill-sails, issue #461). One picture, at most three attempts.

c17d.title: Windmill body without sails, r3, r1 and r2, each on its own guide (3 pictures)
c17d.note_html: Buildings lane, after C17c. Branch art/461-windmill-sails (C17c's commit or later). Issue #461. The author decided on 18 October that the windmill has four views. C17d paints the tower without sails for r3, r1 and r2, each as an edit of its own guide (canvas 1024, scale 8, anchor 512,832; hub offsets r1 (-16,-50), r2 (16,-50), r3 (16,-34)), in the same lane and with the same tests as C17c. C17b's sail cross is turned into each view by an exact transform, so each body must leave the hub exactly at its guide's point. In r1 and r2 the cross is seen from behind: no door, no window, and the stub and plate stand behind the tower. The guides are on the branch claude/art-guides-windmill-coaling, not merged yet; the prompt tells Codex to read them out of that branch into a folder outside its checkout, so they are not committed to the art branch. Nothing is mirrored, sheared or stretched: each view is turned by its own camera.
c17d.label: C17d
c17d.next: The same tower without sails in r3, r1 and r2 (same branch and issue). Three pictures, at most three attempts each.

r7c1.title: People trial: the lumberjack walking away, repainted whole on the grey pose guides (4 pictures)
r7c1.note_html: People lane. Branch art/331-people (exists, head 8005c80 or later). Issue #331. The author chose to repaint whole figures, not only legs. Earlier rounds failed because Codex copies the legs of any painting attached to it, so each pose is now an edit of Art's grey pose mannequin (on develop, assets/source/people-v3-guides/, PR #491: the game's camera and gait, turned 45 degrees), with only the lumberjack's upper body attached for his look. The lumberjack keeps his axe on his shoulder. Every pose is measured: height, soles, the planted foot's slide, the turn, and that P1 and P3 differ. If this trial passes, R7c-2 onward repaint the other back strips and the limping front strips the same way.
r7c1.label: R7c-1
r7c1.next: The lumberjack walking away (branch art/331-people, issue #331). Four pictures, at most twelve calls. The other strips wait for this trial's result.
